  Terse gloss: "To remember or recall to mind; actively recollecting persons, events, or truths, or being passively brought to remembrance."
  Readable gloss: "Rooted in the act of calling something back to awareness, this verb covers the full arc from deliberate recollection to divine passive remembrance. Spanish distinguishes actively remembering — acordarse, acuérdate (remember!) — from being remembered with fue recordada. Twenty-one of twenty-three occurrences are active: Peter 'remembered' Jesus' words (Matt 26:75), God 'remembered' his mercy (Luke 1:54). Two striking passive uses appear when Cornelius' prayers 'were remembered' before God (Acts 10:31) and Babylon 'was remembered' for judgment (Rev 16:19)."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "remember, recall to mind"
    Enriched: To actively recall, recollect, or be mindful of a person, event, or divine promise. Spanish acordarse and German gedenket confirm deliberate mental retrieval. Peter remembering Jesus' prediction (Matt 26:75), God remembering his mercy to Abraham's seed (Luke 1:54, 72), and Jesus' instruction to remember at the altar (Matt 5:23) anchor twenty-one occurrences.
    Existing Spanish translations: acordaos, acuérdate, me-acordaré, os-acordáis, recordad, recordamos, recordando, recordar, recordaron, recordé, recordó, recuerda, recuerdes, se-acordaron
  Sense 2: "be remembered, be called to mind"
    Enriched: To be remembered or called to mind in a passive construction, often as a divine passive where God is the implied agent. Spanish fue recordada and fueron recordadas mark this voice distinctly. Cornelius' prayers 'were remembered' before God (Acts 10:31) and great Babylon 'was remembered' before God to receive judgment (Rev 16:19) — only two occurrences, but theologically rich.
    Existing Spanish translations: fue-recordada, fueron-recordadas
